data.problem: Expose OpenCode tools (built-ins, plugin tools, MCP tools) to Claude Agent SDK with correct schema, metadata, and execution wiring.
constraints: Explore phase only: no implementation or work items.
Reuse existing tool registry and MCP integration where possible.
Preserve permissions + plugin hooks around tool execution.
Tool schemas must be compatible with Claude Agent SDK tool format.
Tool outputs may need truncation and attachments handling.

options.name: Adapter-only tool catalog
options.approach: Create an adapter that transforms ToolRegistry.tools() and MCP.tools() outputs into Claude Agent SDK tool schema (name/description/input_schema). Reuse current execute wrappers from SessionPrompt.resolveTools for execution calls.
options.what_we_learn: Schema compatibility gaps, which metadata fields Claude requires, and how MCP tool outputs map to Claude tool results.
options.risk_if_wrong: May miss execution context or permission flows needed outside SessionPrompt.

options.name: Server endpoints for tool list + execute
options.approach: Add an API that returns the tool catalog and provides a tool execution endpoint using the same Tool.Context and Plugin hooks as SessionPrompt. Claude SDK calls the API instead of direct in-process tool execution.
options.what_we_learn: End-to-end exposure model (auth/permissions, execution results) and how external clients integrate with tools.
options.risk_if_wrong: More surface area and potential auth complexity if the SDK runs outside opencode runtime.

options.name: MCP-first standardization
options.approach: Expose internal tools as MCP tools (local server), then consume MCP tools in Claude Agent SDK. Make MCP the single tool contract boundary.
options.what_we_learn: Standard MCP tool schema compatibility and whether MCP is a stable cross-SDK tool boundary.
options.risk_if_wrong: Larger architecture shift and more moving parts (MCP client/server management).

data.recommendation: Option 1 because it reuses the current tool registry and execution wiring with the smallest surface area, giving the fastest feedback on schema and metadata compatibility.
